items.title: The fx adapter now runs the harness on the host
items.summary: The fx adapter for the AI SDK’s HarnessAgent now runs the harness and model requests in the same process as your application. Built-in filesystem and shell operations remain isolated in the sandbox. The adapter uses libfx , the TypeScript library for fx. It no longer needs to install fx inside the sandbox, run a sandbox bridge, or expose a sandbox port. Model credentials stay on the host rather than being forwarded into the sandbox. The rewrite also adds: Built-in tool filtering: choose which built-in tools the agent can use Mid-turn steering: send new instructions while a turn is running Structured output: generate responses that match a schema Image tool results: return images to the model through toModelOutput() Sessions can be saved and resumed in a new host process. Update @ai-sdk/harness-fx to the latest version to use the new adapter. Learn more in the fx harness documentation . Read more

items.title: Vercel Sandbox commands now support stdin
items.summary: Vercel Sandbox now lets you send input to running commands through standard input (stdin). Use it to exchange messages with stdio MCP servers such as agent-browser , or send data to other command-line programs while they run. In the TypeScript SDK, set stdin: true and detached: true in runCommand() . Use writeStdin() to send input and closeStdin() when you’re done: You can also set stdin to a Node.js readable stream, such as process.stdin . The SDK forwards the stream’s data and closes the command’s standard input when the stream ends. In the Python SDK, set stdin=subprocess.PIPE and send input with server.stdin.send() . Call communicate() to close stdin, collect remaining output, and wait for the process to exit: For commands that receive all their input at once, you can pass input directly to Python’s run_process() . Read the Sandbox documentation to get started. Read more

items.title: GPT-6.1 Terra now available on AI Gateway
items.summary: GPT-6.1 Terra from OpenAI is now available on AI Gateway . GPT-6.1 Terra is a fast model for visual reasoning, computer use, and writing, and it improves on the previous Terra model in visual reasoning, factual accuracy, and coding. It suits high-volume work in documents and desktop apps, such as filling out forms, interpreting technical drawings, or entering invoice details into accounting software. OpenAI still recommends its larger GPT-6 models for the most complex coding tasks. The model accepts text and images and returns text, with a context window of more than 1M tokens. It supports configurable reasoning effort , structured outputs , tool calling, and implicit and explicit prompt caching . For latency-sensitive work, fast mode is available as openai/gpt-6.1-terra-fast . GPT-6.1 Terra works with the AI SDK , the OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions API , the Responses API , and coding agents connected to AI Gateway. Use openai/gpt-6.1-terra as the model name: To use it in Codex, Cursor, and more, install the latest Vercel CLI and run setup: Then select openai/gpt-6.1-terra in the agent. See the coding agents guide for details. Try GPT-6.1 Terra in the model playground . AI Gateway provides a unified API for calling models, tracking usage and cost, and configuring retries, failover, and performance optimizations for higher-than-provider uptime. It includes built-in custom reporting , Zero Data Retention support , budgets for API keys , routing rules , and more. AI Gateway reflects provider pricing with no markup and does not charge a platform fee on inference, including on Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) requests.
